# Silent Zero OS

> Bare minimum. Verified. Real-time. An OS for the AI era. A working paper: a bootloader, a formally verified microkernel and the bare minimum to run AI agents safely and in real time, built entirely from existing open source.

This is a design, not a release: the paper makes the argument and says what is proven, tested or assumed. Text and figures are CC BY 4.0, code is BSD-2-Clause. The wiki is written by a language model from the project's sources; every page states its review status. Each wiki page has a clean Markdown version at its address plus `.md` (`page.html` is `page.html.md`).

## Paper

- [Silent Zero OS, working paper (v0.17)](https://silentzero.ooo/silent-zero.pdf): the full paper as PDF, always the newest version
- [The paper as a web page](https://silentzero.ooo/): the same argument with a short summary first, in English (header also in German, French, Spanish, Italian)

## Wiki

- [Wiki index](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/index.html.md): how the wiki is made, and the catalogue of all pages

## Design

- [Drivers](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/drivers.html.md): user-mode drivers, the first verified Ethernet driver, DMA and the IOMMU as assumed, attacked in 2019 although enabled.
- [Real-time loops](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/real-time-loops.html.md): the loops that move the motors: asynchronous chunks from slow models, observed timings, no proven bound yet.
- [Root of trust and firmware](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/root-of-trust.html.md): the firmware below the kernel on Arm, RISC-V, PC and Raspberry Pi; OpenTitan, Caliptra, DICE; all assumed in the paper’s terms.
- [The bootloader](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/bootloader.html.md): where the Silent Zero loader sits on each platform, signed and measured boot, proofs about boot code so far; the loader itself unproven.
- [The broker](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/broker.html.md): the only component that hands out authority: capability patterns, CaMeL and FIDES, why model-based defences fail; nothing proven yet.
- [The kernel](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/kernel.html.md): seL4 with MCS as the Silent Zero kernel: proven (C-level correctness; MCS functional correctness on RISC-V), not stated for MCS (integrity, confidentiality), tested (HACMS), assumed (boot, IOMMU); no WCET bound on any 64-bit core yet; the roadmap dates MCS on AArch64 to Q3 2027.
- [The safety path](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/safety-path.html.md): Simplex in Silent Zero: the agent proposes, the loop disposes; tested, not proven; the paper’s 2001 date disputed by a 1994 origin.
- [The static system](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/design/static-system.html.md): one description, one image: what Microkit checks, what is not proved, and the run-time swap in LionsOS, the kernel underneath.

## Concepts

- [Action chunking](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/action-chunking.html.md): slow robot models emitting action sequences for a fast loop; no bound on delay.
- [AI vulnerability discovery](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/ai-vulnerability-discovery.html.md): AI models finding software flaws at scale: DARPA’s challenge and Anthropic’s figures, the bottleneck moving to patching.
- [Confused deputy](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/confused-deputy.html.md): a program misusing one party’s authority for another’s request; capabilities as the remedy.
- [Functional correctness](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/functional-correctness.html.md): what seL4’s refinement proof gives, what it assumes, where it holds.
- [Information-flow control](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/information-flow-control.html.md): labels for where data came from and who may see it; FIDES and CaMeL for agents; explicit flows only.
- [IOMMU](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/iommu.html.md): the memory management unit for devices: what it limits, and the 2019 attacks that worked although it was on.
- [Measured boot](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/measured-boot.html.md): each stage records what runs next; TPM and DICE; a verified DICE implementation.
- [Memory-safe code](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/memory-safe-code.html.md): new code in Rust instead of C: Android’s memory-safety flaws below 20 % in 2025; the hardening rival to a verified base.
- [Mixed criticality](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/mixed-criticality.html.md): software of different criticality on one platform; processor time as a capability in seL4 MCS.
- [Object capabilities](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/object-capabilities.html.md): references that both designate and authorise; permission versus authority; caretaker and membrane.
- [Prompt injection](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/prompt-injection.html.md): instructions hidden in data an agent reads; heuristic defences fail, defences around the model hold within limits.
- [Proof automation](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/proof-automation.html.md): machines proposing proof steps, Isabelle checking them; 77.6 % of a seL4 benchmark sample; Verus as a faster verifier. PROMISE as a second method; AutoVerus for Rust.
- [RISC-V](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/risc-v.html.md): the open instruction set: what is open (the ISA) and what need not be (cores, chips, boards); privilege levels and the SBI.
- [Simplex architecture](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/simplex.html.md): a simple safe controller guarding an untrusted one; tested with learned controllers.
- [Time protection](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/time-protection.html.md): closing timing channels between domains; prototypes on CVA6, proof for seL4 in progress.
- [Verified boot](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/verified-boot.html.md): each stage checks the next against a key the attacker cannot change; proofs about boot code so far.
- [WCET analysis](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/concepts/wcet-analysis.html.md): upper bounds on execution time, what they need, and where seL4 stands.

## Systems

- [agentOS](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/agentos.html.md): seL4-based I/O platform for agents: device-owning domains, Linux and FreeBSD guests under QEMU; agent services not yet booted.
- [CHERIoT](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/cheriot.html.md): CHERI capabilities on small RISC-V cores with its own RTOS: memory safety in hardware, measured, not proven; CHERI for RISC-V “being standardised” in 2026.
- [Cohesix](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/cohesix.html.md): seL4-based control layer for edge AI fleets: a Queen decides what hosts’ models may do; landing page only.
- [coreboot](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/coreboot.html.md): open firmware in stages with a fixed payload; verified and measured boot; closed vendor parts on x86.
- [CVA6](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/cva6.html.md): open 64-bit RISC-V core whose design lets latency bounds be proved; fence.t prototype.
- [KataOS](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/kataos.html.md): Google’s seL4 and Rust OS for machine-learning devices, 2022; OpenTitan in its Sparrow plan.
- [Landlock](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/landlock.html.md): Linux sandbox a process applies to itself: filesystem, network, capability and namespace rules; part of the hardened-Linux route.
- [LionsOS](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/lionsos.html.md): static OS from small components on seL4 and Microkit; first driver verified.
- [Microkit](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/microkit.html.md): the build system for static seL4 systems: protection domains, channels, budgets, one image.
- [OpenSBI](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/opensbi.html.md): RISC-V firmware in machine mode below the kernel.
- [OpenTitan](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/opentitan.html.md): open-source silicon root of trust, shipping in Chromebooks since March 2026.
- [PREEMPT_RT](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/preempt-rt.html.md): the Linux real-time configuration: preemptible kernel, threaded interrupts; no latency bound stated.
- [Raspberry Pi](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/raspberry-pi.html.md): the pib’s board: closed ROM and EEPROM boot, secure-boot key in OTP on the Pi 4, seL4 verified without MCS.
- [seL4](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/sel4.html.md): the verified microkernel Silent Zero builds on: proofs per architecture and platform, cost, MCS, timing, HACMS.
- [SiFive and the HiFive boards](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/sifive-hifive.html.md): SiFive and its boards: the discontinued HiFive Unleashed with seL4’s MCS proof, the HiFive Premier P550 one can buy.
- [Trusted Firmware-A](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/tf-a.html.md): Arm’s reference firmware; BL31 stays resident at EL3 below the kernel.
- [Verus](https://silentzero.ooo/wiki/systems/verus.html.md): verifier for Rust code with SMT solving; case studies, no kernel; AutoVerus writes proofs for it.
